evaluations.rationale: The incumbent has direct local evidence: a disabled account with an intact identifier parsed successfully while enabled and project-role controls passed. It remains the baseline to repair but does not specify patch placement or error-order regression, so it is deferred.

Selected. It gives the minimal placement in the account branch and a matrix that separates disabled-state rejection from identifier revocation. The earlier observation supplies the vulnerable baseline, so one action can test the repair and lifecycle controls.

Deferred and folded into the selected regression matrix. Checking after password-time validation also rejects the token, but the error becomes time-specific. The same matrix can include a changed-password control without choosing this placement.
Deferred, not refuted. The earlier test already showed a project-role token accepted independently, so the expected result is supported before the repair. It is retained as a post-repair regression.

Deferred, not refuted. Middleware propagation is a real downstream boundary, but the server fixture is larger than the package-level repair check and the parser already returns an error. It is a plausible later robustness check.

Deferred, not refuted. Concurrent toggling is a distinct concern, but the parser receives account copies and the new predicate adds no shared mutable state. Lower value than patch application and lifecycle regression.
